To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the majority of students are not satisfied with their university education, (2) the majority of teachers are not satisfied with the way they are treated by their university, and (3) the majority of both students and teachers believe that the quality of education in their university is not satisfactory.

the ways in which the cultural and political practices of higher education reproduce and challenge forms of domination.
the way higher education is implicated in the construction and reproduction of social difference.
the ways in which people are produced as particular kinds of subjects, and how these processes are linked to broader historical developments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
anthropologists are beginning to make strangers at home.
anthropology has a great deal to offer the study of higher educational institutions, but that it is only just beginning to do so.
anthropological research in higher education is a promising field of study, but one that is in need of more systematic development.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are interested in how the university is a site of struggle and how the struggle is conducted through the production and reproduction of knowledge.

we are concerned with the ways in which the university is implicated in the production of subjects, and how this production is linked to the production of knowledge, power, subjectivity and the social order.

we have been trying to explore how higher education is involved in the production, maintenance and contestation of the cultural and social order of the nation-state, and in the process, how higher education itself becomes a site of contestation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we must be more attentive to the ways in which the university is a site of social and cultural production and reproduction, as well as a site of struggle and transformation.

the study of higher educational institutions and the students and faculty who inhabit them can be enriched by a critical engagement with the insights of cultural anthropology and the anthropological study of higher education.

we need to be more attentive to the ways in which the university is implicated in the production of the social, and that we need to develop ways of studying this process that are attentive to the ways that the university both produces and is produced by social and economic relations.
